title: Coherent inverse over a nerve with only identity isomorphisms
statement: Use quasicategories, nerves of ordinary categories, coherent functors, functor equivalences and coherent natural equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in fixed universes containing the data. Let $B$ be an ordinary category in which every isomorphism is an identity, and put $S=N(B)$. Let $p:X\to S$ and $q:Y\to S$ be coherent functors from quasicategories and let $F:X\to Y$ satisfy $qF=p$ as simplicial maps. Suppose $F$ is a functor equivalence, so that there are a coherent quasi-inverse $G:Y\to X$ and coherent natural equivalences $GF\simeq\mathrm{id}_X$ and $FG\simeq\mathrm{id}_Y$. Then these same data satisfy $pG=q$ as simplicial maps, and each unit and counit equivalence projects to the constant identity transformation of $p$ or $q$. In particular $F$ is an equivalence over the fixed simplicial base $S$. For any simplicial set $K$ in the ambient universe and specified $a:K\to S$, postcomposition of these inverse data gives a functor equivalence between the simplicial sets of functors $K\to X$ and $K\to Y$ with composite exactly $a$ and transformations over its identity, whenever these simplicial sets are quasicategories. No fibration hypothesis is needed for the strict-base identities.

source.place: step 5, strict-base inverse argument (HTT section 1.2.7, coherent equivalences projected to ordinary nerves). Agent-formulated lemma extracted from the retained proof, not a verbatim source theorem. The indicated source is not archived in literature; WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Choose the specified natural equivalences $\alpha:GF\to\mathrm{id}_X$ and $\beta:FG\to\mathrm{id}_Y$, with their inverse edges and the two inverse $2$-simplices for each, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Evaluate these simplices at any vertex, then apply $p$ or $q$. Faces and degeneracies are preserved, so each projected component has a two-sided inverse in $B$: a $2$-simplex of $N(B)$ is exactly a composable pair together with its composite. Every such component is therefore an isomorphism, hence an identity by the hypothesis on $B$. This applies to the inverse edges as well. In particular $pGF(x)=p(x)$ and $qFG(y)=q(y)$ on vertices.

source.place: Section 1.2.7, Notation 1.2.7.2 (printed p. 39), for internal functor objects and natural equivalences only; the strict-base argument below is agent-written from the explicit nerve and inverse-triangle definitions, not a quoted HTT theorem.

proof.text: Write $H=q\beta:Y\times\Delta^1\to N(B)$; its endpoints are $qFG=pG$ and $q$. Its vertical edge at each vertex $y$ is an identity by step 1. For an edge $e:y\to y'$ of $Y$, the two triangles in $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ with vertices $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$ and $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$ show that the image of the diagonal is respectively $pG(e)$ followed by an identity and an identity followed by $q(e)$. Thus $pG(e)=q(e)$, and this is also the image of the diagonal. Every edge of $Y\times\Delta^1$ is horizontal, vertical or of this diagonal form, including degenerate $e$. Hence $H$ agrees with $q\,\mathrm{pr}_Y$ on vertices and edges. By the nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $n$-simplex is a functor $[n]\to B$, determined by its objects and consecutive arrows. Applying this observation to every simplex proves $H=q\,\mathrm{pr}_Y$ in all degrees. Its endpoint restrictions give $pG=q$ as simplicial maps, and $q\beta$ is exactly the constant identity transformation.

source.place: Section 1.2.7, Notation 1.2.7.2 (printed p. 39), for internal functor objects and natural equivalences only; the strict-base argument below is agent-written from the explicit nerve and inverse-triangle definitions, not a quoted HTT theorem.

proof.text: For $J=p\alpha:X\times\Delta^1\to N(B)$ both endpoints are now $p$: indeed $pGF=qF=p$ by step 2 and the given equality $qF=p$. The vertical edges are identities by step 1. For each $e:x\to x'$, the same two product triangles give image $p(e)$ for the diagonal and for both horizontal edges. Thus $J$ and $p\,\mathrm{pr}_X$ have the same vertices and edges, and equality of their consecutive-arrow chains gives equality on every simplex. Consequently $p\alpha$ is the constant identity transformation of $p$. This uses only the explicit nerve and product definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Section 1.2.7, Notation 1.2.7.2 (printed p. 39), for internal functor objects and natural equivalences only; the strict-base argument below is agent-written from the explicit nerve and inverse-triangle definitions, not a quoted HTT theorem.

proof.text: The inverse transformations of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ also project constantly: their vertical edges are identities by step 1, and the product-triangle calculation of steps 2 and 3 applies with the endpoint order reversed. Consider either inverse-triangle witness, now a map $T\times\Delta^2\to N(B)$ with $T=X$ or $Y$ after projection. Its three parameter edges restrict to these constant projected transformations or a degenerate identity transformation. For any edge $e$ of $T$, and any parameter edge $i\to j$ of $\Delta^2$, restriction along $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to T\times\Delta^2$ gives the same two triangles. The mixed edge therefore maps to $p(e)$ or $q(e)$; vertical edges map to identities. Every vertex and edge is consequently that of the base map composed with $\mathrm{pr}_T$, so every simplex is too by the nerve definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The inverse edges and their actual two inverse witnesses are thus over the identity base. Together with $qF=p$ and $pG=q$, these same data exhibit the claimed equivalence over $S$.

source.place: Section 1.2.7, Notation 1.2.7.2 (printed p. 39), for internal functor objects and natural equivalences only; the strict-base argument below is agent-written from the explicit nerve and inverse-triangle definitions, not a quoted HTT theorem.

proof.text: Fix $a:K\to S$. Spell out the relative simplicial sets using the internal-hom formula of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: $X_a$ has $n$-simplices $u:K\times\Delta^n\to X$ satisfying $pu=a\,\mathrm{pr}_K$, and $Y_a$ is defined similarly with $q$. Restriction preserves this equality. The formulas $F_a(u)=Fu$ and $G_a(v)=Gv$ commute with all simplicial operators and land in $Y_a$ and $X_a$, respectively, because $qF=p$ and $pG=q$. Thus the specified functors act on every simplex over exactly the prescribed base map.

source.place: Section 1.2.7, Notation 1.2.7.2 (printed p. 39), for internal functor objects and natural equivalences only; the strict-base argument below is agent-written from the explicit nerve and inverse-triangle definitions, not a quoted HTT theorem.

proof.text: The transformation on $X_a$ induced by $\alpha$ is the map $X_a\times\Delta^1\to X_a$ whose value on an $n$-simplex $(u,t)$, $t:\Delta^n\to\Delta^1$, is the map $(k,z)\mapsto\alpha(u(k,z),t(z))$ from $K\times\Delta^n$ to $X$. Its base is $a(k)$ by step 3. This formula commutes with restriction in $n$, and its endpoints are $G_aF_a$ and the identity. Apply the identical formula to $\beta$ on $Y_a$, to their inverse edges, and to each inverse $2$-simplex (replacing $t$ by a map to $\Delta^2$). Step 4 makes every resulting simplex lie over $a$, and the face identities remain the original inverse-triangle identities. They therefore exhibit coherent natural equivalences $G_aF_a\simeq\mathrm{id}_{X_a}$ and $F_aG_a\simeq\mathrm{id}_{Y_a}$ by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. When $X_a,Y_a$ are quasicategories as assumed, this is precisely a functor equivalence. No filler, lifting or fibration assertion was used.

lean.statement: theorem equivalence_over_gaunt_nerve (B : Type u) [Category.{v} B] (hB : ∀ (x y : B) (i : x ≅ y), ∃ h : x = y, i.hom = eqToHom h) {X Y : SSet.{max u v}} [Quasicategory X] [Quasicategory Y] (p : X ⟶ nerve B) (q : Y ⟶ nerve B) (F : X ⟶ Y) (G : Y ⟶ X) (hF : F ≫ q = p) (α : SpecifiedNaturalEquivalence (F ≫ G) (𝟙 X)) (β : SpecifiedNaturalEquivalence (G ≫ F) (𝟙 Y)) : ∃ hG : G ≫ p = q, α.IsOver p p ∧ β.IsOver q q ∧ ∀ (K : SSet.{max u v}) (a : K ⟶ nerve B), Quasicategory (pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) (diagramVertex a)) ((ihom K).map p)) → Quasicategory (pullback (SSet.const (X := Δ[0]) (diagramVertex a)) ((ihom K).map q)) → ∃ (αa : SpecifiedNaturalEquivalence (gauntRelativePostcomposition p q F hF a ≫ gauntRelativePostcomposition q p G hG a) (𝟙 _)) (βa : SpecifiedNaturalEquivalence (gauntRelativePostcomposition q p G hG a ≫ gauntRelativePostcomposition p q F hF a) (𝟙 _)), α.IsInduced αa (pullback.snd _ _) ∧ β.IsInduced βa (pullback.snd _ _) ∧ IsFunctorEquivalence (gauntRelativePostcomposition p q F hF a)
lean.note: Retains the supplied inverse, both natural-equivalence edges, their inverse edges and all inverse triangles. Relative postcomposition is the canonical Mathlib pullback.map; IsInduced specifies the evaluation of each original witness on every simplex. Auxiliary records merely expose witnesses of the recorded dependency predicates.
